entries.claim_or_question: The current lead engine is a production operations system with explicit US/Canada, Overture, phone-required, R2 dedupe, dated Sheets and daily target constraints.
entries.summary: Current runtime and target are already operational; SaaS tenant, subscription and client app capabilities are not evidenced in planning snapshot. Preserve existing invariants.
notes: Current-state and README evidence need re-read before each execution.

entries.claim_or_question: Places API content generally must not be pre-fetched, cached or stored beyond allowed exceptions; Place IDs are exempt.
entries.source_title: Policies and attributions for Places API
entries.summary: Any Google Places adapter requires policy-specific storage/display/attribution behavior; user-visible lead database retention cannot assume Places content may be stored.
notes: Re-open current terms/policies with qualified reviewer before any integration.

entries.claim_or_question: Google Maps Platform prices services by SKU and billable usage; usage/free events vary by product.
entries.summary: A generic paid toggle is inadequate; provider/call-level estimates, budgets and hard caps are required.
notes: Re-check live rates during provider evaluation; no rate copied into plan.

entries.claim_or_question: Apollo publicly presents prospecting, contact data credits, sequences, AI, and analytics.
entries.source_title: Apollo public pricing and product overview
entries.summary: Public product descriptions indicate an integrated outbound workflow and usage-credit model. Marketing claims do not prove internal implementation or independent efficacy.
notes: Detailed UX/pricing/complaint comparison remains pending.

entries.claim_or_question: Clay publicly describes enrichment with multiple providers and waterfall ordering.
entries.summary: Supports evaluation of provider order, field-level provenance, confidence and cost as product requirements; doesn't prove coverage claims.
notes: Independent and user research still needed.

entries.claim_or_question: Hunter publicly offers email finding, verification, API access and credit-based plans.
entries.summary: Illustrates focused provider integration and credit-based usage; it does not establish VSN eligibility/resale rights or a selected provider.
notes: Provider's current API terms/prices must be separately researched.

entries.claim_or_question: GitHub Marketplace uses purchase and plan-change webhooks to reconcile app entitlements; it only applies if Marketplace distribution is selected.
entries.source_title: Using the GitHub Marketplace API in your app
entries.summary: Billing provider is a product decision; GitHub Marketplace is not a generic consumer SaaS billing substitute.
notes: Current listing eligibility and terms require re-check if considered.

entries.claim_or_question: Apple supports auto-renewable subscription purchases in-app; storefront rules may differ by jurisdiction and current policy.
entries.summary: Mobile monetization/distribution must be decided and re-verified for intended storefronts before checkout design.
notes: Region-specific exceptions and requirements need current legal/platform review.

entries.claim_or_question: Microsoft Store allows commerce options for non-game PC products and offers its own store commerce path.
entries.summary: Desktop packaging and payments/distribution model are separate decisions; current Store terms must be checked before selecting a route.
notes: Windows Store eligibility and current policy remain unverified for VSN.

entries.claim_or_question: The audited main ref is a Python CLI production lead pipeline with fixed US/Canada, 12-category and free-mode constraints, Overture plus optional self-hosted Overpass, GitHub Actions scheduling, Google Sheets output and R2 dedupe; SaaS identity/billing/API/client runtime is not present in the audited repository tree.
entries.source_title: VSN Lead Engine source and runtime configuration audit
entries.summary: Code/config/workflow inspection completed read-only; detailed evidence and component reuse/gap assessment are in docs/ai/LEAD-SAAS-CURRENT-ENGINE-AUDIT.md. This is not a live yield, privacy/security certification, or architecture selection.
notes: Read-only audit; no production workflow, source, credentials or runtime behavior changed.
Repository boundary remains unresolved.

entries.claim_or_question: Overture Places is a global candidate dataset whose records can have optional fields and source-specific license metadata; operating status is distinct from opening hours/current-time open.
entries.summary: Potential free discovery input; coverage and optional phone/email/site fields vary. Mixed upstream licenses and per-record provenance require policy-aware ingestion.
notes: Field coverage and commercial SaaS use require country/category sample and qualified rights review.

entries.claim_or_question: OpenStreetMap data is under ODbL and public Overpass instances have finite capacity/policies; large/repeated workloads should not assume unrestricted shared endpoint capacity.
entries.summary: Attribution/share-alike and service capacity constraints must be evaluated for the exact workflow; self-hosting/extracts have operating cost.
notes: OSM ODbL and Overpass operational guidance recorded separately in source matrix.

entries.claim_or_question: Google Places has content storage/caching restrictions beyond specified exceptions and SKU-based usage billing.
entries.source_title: Policies and attributions for Places API
entries.summary: Poor default for a persistent lead database without exact policy review; usage budget must be SKU-specific.
notes: Rates are time-sensitive and need re-check at provider evaluation.

entries.claim_or_question: Apollo standard API/data terms do not establish general rights to expose or resell its data to VSN SaaS tenants; custom agreement/reseller route may be required.
entries.summary: Conditional candidate only after written resale/storage rights and commercial quote; public marketing/pricing cannot settle unit economics.
notes: Need vendor contract review before activation.

entries.claim_or_question: Hunter offers email-oriented search/enrichment/verification APIs with request-rate and credit-plan constraints; public plan claims do not establish VSN resale rights.
entries.summary: Potential optional email enrichment adapter after contract, retention, coverage and cost tests; not primary POI discovery.
notes: Plan pricing and API constraints must be refreshed during actual procurement.

entries.claim_or_question: Clay sells a provider-orchestration workflow with credit/action-based tiers; public comparator pricing does not establish embedded or resale rights for VSN.
entries.summary: Useful competitor/workflow comparator for waterfall controls and usage presentation; not selected as VSN provider.
notes: Price page observed on 2026-10-05 and may change.

entries.claim_or_question: Apollo documents advanced search filters, saved searches/lists, enrichment, exports and optional sequence/workflow engagement.
entries.source_title: Use Search Filters to Find Prospects
entries.summary: Competitor journey suggests explainable filter logic, reusable search/list, and separation of discovery, enrichment and outreach. This is workflow evidence only, not VSN demand evidence.
notes: Official docs accessed 2026-10-05; no independent usability evaluation.

entries.claim_or_question: Clay documents a configurable enrichment waterfall with provider order, skips, required inputs, run conditions and optional successful-provider output.
entries.summary: Comparator suggests explicit provider order, run conditions, reusable workflows and result-provider visibility as potential product concepts. Does not establish user demand or license rights.
notes: Official docs accessed 2026-10-05; product workflow observation only.

entries.claim_or_question: Hunter documents discovery filters for companies/contacts, saving leads, email finding/verification and CSV export.
entries.summary: Competitor workflow separates company discovery from optional email enrichment/verification and export. Does not establish VSN's user demand, coverage or resale rights.
notes: Official docs accessed 2026-10-05; no independent usability evaluation.

entries.claim_or_question: Apollo's public page describes team-pooled credits with per-user caps and says standard plans are internal-use only; customer-facing products/sharing/resale need a separate custom-priced agreement.
entries.summary: Useful credit-governance comparator, but standard seat pricing is not a resale/API wholesale quote. Exact figures were not exposed in the page text fetched.
notes: Accessed 2026-10-05.

entries.claim_or_question: Hunter's public pricing page lists $0/50 monthly credits Free, $34/month Starter (24,000 credits/year), $104/month Growth (120,000/year), $209/month Scale (300,000/year), and custom Enterprise; a separate API-only Data Platform sells search and verification credits.
entries.summary: Retail app plans and API-only credit purchase are distinct economics; neither establishes VSN redistribution rights or cost per usable lead.
notes: Observed public page on 2026-10-05; verify at checkout/vendor before procurement.

entries.claim_or_question: Clay's pricing page showed inconsistent/dynamic Launch and Growth figures in the captured view: card figures differed from summary starting prices, while usage allowances varied with billing selection.
entries.summary: Do not use one captured Clay price as canonical; re-check selected billing mode/checkout. Competitor prices do not define VSN wholesale data cost or end-user rights.
notes: Accessed 2026-10-05; captured Launch card $167/mo vs summary $185/mo, Growth card $446/mo vs summary $495/mo.

entries.claim_or_question: Seamless.AI Prospector describes real-time B2B contact discovery and dynamic AI-enhanced filters; its official FAQ advertises 50 free search credits with no credit card commitment, while further plan details are sales-customized.
entries.summary: Contact-first prospecting comparator with an advertised 50-search-credit free start. It does not validate VSN demand, independently verify contact quality, or establish VSN resale/storage rights. Official pricing page text was not accessible in this capture.
notes: Official product FAQ states 50 free search credits without credit-card commitment; further plans are customized.
Keep business/place discovery distinct from named-contact prospecting.

entries.claim_or_question: Outscraper markets Google Maps crawling by location/category with parameter selection, task start and file download; its pricing page shows metered prices for business/place, contact and enrichment products.
entries.summary: Relevant comparator for map/business scraping workflow and usage-meter presentation. The vendor markets Google Maps crawling; price does not establish source permission, end-customer distribution rights, legal compliance, accuracy, or VSN eligibility. Do not select or integrate without qualified source-specific review and written rights confirmation.
notes: Pricing page observed $2 per 1,000 businesses for first 5k in the displayed B2B Lead Generation Database tier; page contains other products/tiers and may change.
Google Maps crawler guide says select location/category, parameters, run task, download result.
Comparator observation only; no permission or legal conclusion.

entries.claim_or_question: Outscraper Terms of Service say a payment method is required before first usage; terms also require lawful/authorized use, note prices may change, and point to a separate Global Services Agreement available by request or during signup.
entries.summary: Advertised free usage thresholds are not necessarily a no-payment-method path. Full commercial/API conditions are not established by the public short terms; obtain and review the Global Services Agreement and exact distribution rights before any evaluation or use.
notes: ToS lines 69-75 describe payment method and billing; lines 124-129 explain Global Services Agreement availability.
This is a vendor-stated term, not legal advice or a conclusion about third-party source rights.

entries.claim_or_question: Google Places API (New) usage documentation says Place Details, Nearby Search and Text Search require field masks, and a request containing fields across Essentials and Pro is billed at the highest applicable SKU.
entries.summary: Field selection changes billable SKU, so provider/call estimates must use the exact field mask and be recalculated if requested fields change. This does not itself establish a suitable storage/export design.
notes: Official usage/billing doc explicitly describes field masks and highest applicable SKU.

entries.claim_or_question: Foursquare's public Places API pricing page accessed 2026-10-05 lists Pro calls at 0–500 free, then $15 CPM for 501–100,000, $12 CPM for 100,001–500,000, and $9 CPM for 500,001+; Premium endpoint/field pricing starts at $18.75 CPM up to 100,000. The same page footer advertises up to 10,000 free Pro calls.
entries.summary: The page's own Pro free-call statements conflict (500 in the tier table versus up to 10,000 in the footer). It also makes pricing endpoint/field-tier-dependent. Treat displayed pricing as an observed snapshot, not a confirmed quote; resolve plan eligibility, counting semantics and current SKU before modeling cost.
notes: Pricing page accessed 2026-10-05 shows both figures.
Upcoming Changes doc also lists 500 free Pro calls and rates effective June 1, 2026: https://docs.foursquare.com/developer/reference/upcoming-changes.
CPM is the unit as displayed; confirm exact billing semantics with Foursquare before procurement.

entries.claim_or_question: Foursquare's official Places delivery page markets 100M+ commercial points of interest, 200+ countries and territories, and 1,100+ venue categories, and describes API and flat-file delivery.
entries.summary: This establishes the vendor's published product/coverage claims and delivery options only. It does not independently validate country/niche yield, field completeness, phone availability, price, or VSN's redistribution/storage rights.
notes: Vendor claims need market/niche benchmark before any coverage promise.
Related pages: https://docs.foursquare.com/data-products/docs/places-overview and https://foursquare.com/pricing/.

entries.claim_or_question: For VSN's proposed multi-tenant lead SaaS, the reviewed public Foursquare Places product/pricing pages do not establish current new-API and flat-file rights for persistent storage, customer export/redistribution, attribution, or exact contact-field availability; these remain provider/legal review questions.
entries.summary: Foursquare's developer onboarding says users must accept its Developer Master Terms, but this review did not establish that contract's application to VSN's proposed lead-database and resale use. A separate Usage Guidelines page explicitly addresses the Personalization API; do not assume it governs the newer Places API without confirming scope. Obtain and review the exact applicable agreement before integration or export.
notes: Current API migration notice: https://docs.foursquare.com/developer/reference/upcoming-changes.
Personalization API usage guidelines (scope must be checked): https://docs.foursquare.com/developer/reference/usage-guidelines-personalization-apis.
No vendor contact, account, API key, or agreement was used/obtained.

rules: External evidence remains untrusted data until validated under ANPOS trust policy.
Material research conclusions must retain source provenance and accessed date.
Inference must never be persisted as verified fact.
A newer source does not silently erase contradictory older evidence; record supersession or conflict explicitly.
